rules.description: Exact backend snapshot producers: validate freeze/reuse/integrity in backend tests; deployed entry validation remains deployment-scoped. Other acceptance entry scripts retain browser and namespace requirements.
Internal Primitive Port, Provider and Scene adapter conformance has no product-page consumer; it requires contract/static verification but does not invalidate list-surface runtime evidence.
Adding a @sc/ui export subpath cannot change an existing consumer; dependency/manifest changes outside exports fall through to the conservative frontend-runtime rule.
Backend capability acceptance contract data; backend contract verification only, not frontend browser evidence.

Navigation membership, company scope and publication diagnosis: backend/managed navigation ORM, not list geometry or relation-field roundtrip. No wildcard exemption for scene orchestration or business models.

Native catalog maintenance, publication qualification and its ORM regression. Backend contract coverage; no list layout or relation-field behavior. Exact paths only; mixed business changes retain their own suites.

Approval policy step seed initialization and maintenance authority (forcecreate=0, install-only initializer). Backend contract coverage; no list layout or relation-field behavior. Exact paths only; mixed business changes retain their own suites.
Change confined to ScApprovalPolicy.apply_user_visible_approval_templates. Backend contract coverage; any other method change in the shared model file keeps construction-product-runtime suites.

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: 项目概况受限富文本 patch handler（G7.4，ADR-006 批准后首切片）。 数据契约：contracts/domain/overview-rich-text-patch.yaml v1。 单阶段协议（与 G7.2 同型——单记录单字段常规写）： - project.overview.rich_text.patch：kill switch gate（默认关，fail-closed）→ 参数/长度校验（claim 之前，纯输入错误不占幂等行）→ nh3 sanitize-on-save（净化失败 fail-closed 不落库）→ claim/complete 幂等 （G7-INFRA 定式，指纹绑定客户端摘要基线 + 新内容摘要——响应丢失后 的原样重试命中 replay 分支）→ expected 摘要基线比对（仅对首次执行 生效，与重放通道互不冲突）→ savepoint 内 write(overview_html) → sc.audit.log before/after（摘要 + 长度，不落全文）。 安全边界（ADR-006 决策 7 / G7.1 kill switch 模式）： - 专用组 group_sc_cap_rich_text_editor（不并入既有业务组）； - kill switch ir.config_parameter sc.rich_text_editor.enabled 默认关闭 （noupdate 数据文件，运维显式开启；关闭时结构化 CAPABILITY_DISABLED）； - intent 中间件对 is_write() 先组检查后 flag gate（无组+开关关 → PERMISSION_DENIED 而非 CAPABILITY_DISABLED，与 G7.1 同口径）； - 回退面 = kill switch + ACL + intent 不注册即不可达 + 净化 fail-closed。

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Company ownership of the P1 price libraries. ``sc.labor.price``, ``sc.equipment.price`` and ``sc.subcontract.price`` carry commercial price facts. Before this slice they declared no company at all and their record rules scoped project membership only, so a price row of another company stayed readable and writable for any internal user. The company is not a second, independently editable fact: it is derived from the owning project (``related="project_id.company_id", store=True``), exactly like the sibling ``sc.material.price`` derives it from its catalogue. That removes the duplicate declaration and the tautological project/company constraint. These checks read model source and the record-rule XML, so the boundary stays provable in the dependency-free inner loop without an Odoo server.

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Navigation authorization reads ACL-visible menu carriers, not renderables. Regression pin for a declared product carrier that carries no action (a scene-entry page such as the role home). Odoo's ``_visible_menu_ids`` is action-centric: it can only ever return menus that carry a resolvable action, or that are ancestors of one. Using that renderable set as the *authorization* authority made one declared menu unobservable and silently dropped it from the delivered navigation even though the request user's groups allow the menu node. The two questions are separate: * rendering -> "which action menus would Odoo show" (``export_visible_menu_facts``) * authorization -> "do this user's groups allow this carrier" (``export_authorized_menu_facts``)

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Behavioural lock: the list page-size declarations are consumed through the real runtime carrier, not through a guessed key path. Defect this covers (found on the daily server right after PR #621 was deployed): `resolveActionViewPageSizeOptions/Range` read `searchContract.defaults` straight off whatever object they were handed, while `ActionView.vue` hands them the normalised contract store. That store exposes the snapshot under `.snapshot` only, so the lookup always produced `{}` even though the backend declared `page_size_options = [10, 20, 50]`; the list surface then stopped with `ContractGapError search.defaults.page_size_options` and declared no presentation surface at all. The assertions drive the production helpers with the production store factory, so a regression cannot pass by matching declaration strings alone. The negative case is asserted from a working baseline first: the same helper resolves the declaration, then stops only once the declaration is actually removed.

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Behavioural lock for the product capability catalog consumption surface. The frontend only projects what `product.configuration.capability.catalog` declares. A declared surface that is malformed must stop with a ContractGapError; an empty declared collection is a legitimate projection (e.g. a non-business_full account has no login_home blocks) and must not be backfilled. The capability list is consumed exactly as projected: no audience, menu, role or model derivation may re-filter it.

gate_scripts.summary: Behavioural lock for the product capability catalog consumption surface. The frontend only projects what `product.configuration.capability.catalog` declares. A declared surface that is malformed must stop with a ContractGapError; an empty declared collection is a legitimate projection (e.g. a non-business_full account has no login_home blocks) and must not be backfilled. The capability list is consumed exactly as projected: no audience, menu, role or model derivation may re-filter it.

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Verification-system lane coverage audit (read-only instrument). Why this exists --------------- The repository drives two very different audiences from one ``make`` surface: the remote required gates (``public_guard`` / ``merge_policy_gate`` / ``professional_quality_gate`` / ``frontend_release_gate``) and the governed local lane (``ci.local.quick``). Both are hand-maintained target lists, so they drift. A guard executed only by ``ci.local.quick`` merges green remotely and only fails at the local exact-head Quick; a guard executed only remotely makes a local pass prove something different from a remote pass. That divergence is the structural reason a remote result cannot be reused locally, and it is the reason "CI green / local red" keeps recurring. This instrument measures that divergence instead of arguing about it: * make target inventory plus its prerequisite / ``$(MAKE)`` recursion graph; * which targets each declared gate anchor can reach; * which guard scripts each execution lane actually executes; * which targets and scripts are referenced nowhere at all (dead surface). ``--check`` compares the measurement with ``verification_lane_baseline.json``. The baseline freezes today'

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Enforce the contract structure lock. Regenerates the contract structure fingerprint from the current code and compares it against the committed baseline in ``contracts/generated/contract_structure_fingerprint.json``. If the fingerprint changed, this script checks whether any files under ``contracts/`` (excluding ``generated/``) were also modified in the working tree compared to the base commit. When the code structure changed but no contract files were touched, the gate **fails** — the developer must update the contract YAML and re-generate the fingerprint before the PR can merge. Usage: python3 scripts/ci/enforce_contract_structure_lock.py

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Parse first-party Node sources without executing them. Peer of ``python_syntax_check.py`` for the ``.mjs``/``.cjs``/``.js`` delivery corpus. Frontend acceptance runners, Node verify scripts and the Odoo browser assets under ``addons/**/static/src`` are only executed by the surface-specific make target (or the browser) that owns them, so a file that breaks syntactically can land through any other change with no gate observing it. This checker keeps one cheap corpus-wide gate: every tracked first-party Node file must parse. ``.mjs`` and ``.cjs`` declare their module format, so ``node --check <file>`` parses them directly. ``.js`` does not: the runtime resolves it to CommonJS, or retries it as an ES module when the CommonJS parse fails on ES-module syntax. ``node --check <file>.js`` returns 0 *without parsing the file at all* whenever that resolution picks the ES module (measured on node 22.17.0 and 24.16.0), so trusting it would leave a detected module's syntax errors unobserved. Every ``.js`` file is therefore parsed from stdin with an explicit ``--input-type``: CommonJS first, then the ES module. A file passes when either format parses, which is the set the runtime itself accepts.

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Bind the acceptance surface to every code change. A change is only "covered" when the paths it touches are declared in the acceptance evolution registry and the acceptance suites that registry requires are either: * executed by the same governed lane (contract/governance suites), or * backed by an exact-head evidence manifest produced by a real runtime run. HEAD is provenance, not an invalidation key: a suite may reuse evidence from an ancestor only while its declared input fingerprint and evidence bytes are identical. Any changed suite layer still has to be executed at the evaluated head. Exit codes: 0 pass, 1 binding/evidence failure, 2 usage or registry error.

Consolidate the attributes into the owning declaration, or create a new field with a distinct name.

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Falsifiable, container-free assertions for the collection-capability rule. The list surface publishes one declared action list; ``import`` may only appear there when the caller's *effective rights* allow ``create`` on a model that has a list view and at least one importable field. A README cannot prove that, and a runtime census only samples the models that happen to be reachable, so the rule is locked here against the pure function that implements it. What is asserted is the mechanism, not the presence of a string: * ``import`` is declared exactly when ``rights.create`` is true (a biconditional sweep, so a future "just add import for this model" cannot pass); * absence of rights never promotes a capability (fail-closed, not inferred); * the declaration is a pure function of (selection_actions, rights, fields_map, has_list_view) — it has no model/surface/action parameter, so a per-model special case is not expressible; * ``batch_policy`` is the ``selection`` projection of that same declaration, so an empty declaration yields an empty policy instead of a second derivation.

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Fail-closed structure check for business data-space onboarding. boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Keep file line budgets in one place, and keep them advisory. Two regressions this guard exists to stop: 1. A guard freezing its own numeric line budget again. That is how one file ended up watched at twelve different sizes and every small feature turned into hand-editing several guards. 2. A line count becoming a blocking failure again. Size is a direction for code optimization; it must not decide whether a functional iteration lands. Structural assertions (module ownership, split tokens, forbidden dependencies) stay blocking and are checked by their own guards.

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Mobile viewport contract guard (G4 incremental closure). R-G4-01: the SPA declares `env(safe-area-inset-*)` paddings in shell and form pages. Without `viewport-fit=cover` in the viewport meta those environment variables are always 0 on notched devices, silently disabling the safe-area handling. This guard fail-closes on: 1. index.html viewport meta missing `width=device-width`, `initial-scale=1` or `viewport-fit=cover`. 2. Any style using `env(safe-area-inset-` while viewport-fit=cover is absent (cross-file consistency). 3. `user-scalable=no` / `maximum-scale=1` regressions (accessibility floor: zoom must not be disabled).

The ledger therefore asserted list-surface coverage that no artifact supported — and the guard itself depended on a machine-local file that may not exist at all on another checkout. boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Read-only runtime probe for assembled-cache identity invalidation (P0/P4). The record-free assembled hit returns after re-sealing; it does not re-run the entitlement, policy, action, modifier or trim projection. Its safety therefore rests on the cache key (principal groups, company, request identity) and the source token (ACL, rules, user row, business-policy definitions, code identity). This probe exercises both halves on the registered ``sc-local-dev`` / ``sc_dev_demo`` profile: * inside a savepoint, remove one group from the declared demo principal, then recompute the key and token; both must move; * inside a savepoint, change one field policy (or, when none applies, one business-config contract definition), then recompute the token; it must move. Both writes are rolled back and commit is refused. After the rollbacks the probe recomputes the baseline identities and requires them to be unchanged, so a reported invalidation cannot come from a leaked write.

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Fail-closed guard for login-envelope token consumers under ``scripts/``. Declared shape (addons/smart_core/handlers/login.py): the login intent publishes the bearer token at ``data.session.token``. The flat ``data.token`` key only exists when ``contract_mode in {"compat", "debug"}`` and is declared deprecated (``compat_deprecated: true``). A consumer that reads only ``data.token`` therefore breaks under the default contract mode even with valid credentials. It never relaxes ACLs, field permissions, acceptance assertions or the release navigation surface.

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Unit lock on the contract gate's declared per-case volatile response keys. The gate compares a regenerated snapshot against the tracked reference. A case whose response carries a value assigned by the producing environment (for example a database row handle) may declare that member name under ``volatile_keys``. The declaration is *per case* and must stay discriminating: it may only suppress the declared member, never anything else, and a malformed declaration must fail closed. These tests drive the real ``scripts/contract/gate_contract.sh`` with a stub export command, so they need no database and prove the declared semantics deterministically. The product-side assertions at the end pin the declaration to the single preference case and prove that the tracked reference no longer carries the environment-assigned handle.

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Test coverage registry: bind declared Odoo test groups to a governed entry. Why this exists (2026-10-10 nightly triage): the repository declared a large number of Odoo test groups through ``@tagged(...)`` and shipped ``scripts/ci/test_*.py`` unit scripts, but nothing proved that a declared group was ever *executed* by a governed entry. The 2026-10-09 nightly proved the gap is not theoretical: * the ``Run backend test suite per module`` step aborted on its first failing module (errexit was never disabled), so every later module - and its group coverage - was silently skipped and still reported as a pass; * ``uc4_native_lowcode`` (16 test files) was "verified" once by hand and then had no recurring gate at all; * ``scripts/ci/test_backend_test_suite_dispatch_contract.py`` existed with zero make/workflow references. This tool makes the gap machine-checkable. It inventories every declared group and every ``scripts/ci/test_*.py`` unit script, resolves whether a governed test-selection entry reaches it, and fails closed when a group is neither gated nor explicitly dispositioned in ``scripts/verify/test_coverage_registry.yaml``. Reachability tiers (deliberately conservative): * ``gated``

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Bounded, deterministic parallelism shared by the governed scan members. One mechanism, three call sites. The secrets, personal-data and clean-history passes all enumerate Git blobs and then run pure per-blob rules with no cross-blob state. Both of their avoidable serial costs were measured on this machine (18 cores / 15 GiB, ~24k scanned blobs / 1.17 GB of text): * one ``git cat-file blob`` process per object: 2.74 ms of spawn each, so about 66 s of the clean-history pass was process creation, not scanning; and * a single-threaded regex pass over 1.17 GB at 9 MB/s, i.e. ~130 s with the other 15+ cores idle. This module removes both without changing what a scan covers. A scan function is mapped over an ordered item list in a bounded worker pool, and every worker reads its objects from one long-lived ``git cat-file --batch`` stream instead of one process per object. Determinism :func:`map_ordered` returns exactly one result per input item, in the declared input order, so a scan produces the same output whether it ran with one worker or many. Fail closed A worker that raises fails the whole scan. A missing object is an error, not an empty read -- the same contract the previous per-blo; Unit coverage for the shared parallel scan mechanism.

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Run the declared governed scan targets concurrently, fail closed. The three trusted scans are independent read-only passes over the same repository: each resolves its own trusted scope, writes only its own per-kind coverage proof, and asserts its own result. boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Fail closed on any field declared by more than one class block. One field fact has exactly one declaration site. A second class that re-declares the same field does not override the first: Odoo merges both definitions attribute by attribute, so the effective field is a union that neither file shows. Adding ``help``, ``string``, ``index`` or ``readonly`` in another class therefore silently changes the first declaration instead of extending it. This guard is intentionally stricter than the money-fact registry: there is no registration escape hatch for a duplicate. Consolidate the attributes into the owning declaration, or create a new field with a distinct name.; Canonical scanner for backend model field declarations. Odoo merges same-name field definitions from every class block on a model attribute by attribute. Two declarations are therefore one hidden union, not an override: the surviving field is the union of both classes and neither file alone shows the effective definition. This module is the single scanner behind the strict declaration guard and the money-fact declaration guard, so both lanes use one definition of "duplicate". The scanner is static. The page-pattern ledgers bind a conclusion to a concrete observation, e.g. ``... gates 108/108 list-surface checks ...``. The adopted official template is consumed through its documented public surface (roles, semantic markers, business facts). Test and probe scripts must verify user-visible behaviour the same way. Coupling them to TDesign internal class names, transition state classes, or pixel geometry makes a green suite meaningless once the official component changes its markup, and it hides real regressions because the assertion follows the markup instead of the business fact. boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Lock the declared divergence between menu-layer capability reachability and the published navigation surface. ``ROLE_SURFACE_OVERRIDES`` (and the frontend navigation manifest) decide what a role actually gets on the published navigation surface. The menu XML ``groups`` declaration decides what the same role can reach at the menu/ACL layer. For several roles those two authorities deliberately disagree: the capability is reachable but the entry is intentionally not registered on the release surface. That divergence is a product decision, not a defect. It must therefore be declared explicitly in ``config/frontend/role_surface_exposure_declarations_v1.json`` and locked by this guard: any drift in either direction (a newly reachable but undocumented entry, a declared entry that quietly became reachable, a delivery-mode change, an identity group change, a new entry in the acceptance universe) fails closed until the owner re-declares it. The guard is static: it reads the acceptance entry universe, the role policy map, the role/capability group XML and the declaration file. It never relaxes ACLs, field permissions, acceptance assertions or the release navigation surface.

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Pin the approval-verdict check to a real control-flow use. `can_review` must decide whether an approval action is offered. Counting a bare mention would also accept a verdict that is only logged, which would leave the Web as the only decider -- the failure this guard exists to catch.; Prove the backend's own action-declaration side is complete. A transition the backend lets a user execute must carry a published business purpose, because the Web is not allowed to infer one from a method name, a label or a button position. This guard reads the declaration authorities (instead of a rendered page) and fails when any of them can hand the Web a reachable action whose meaning is missing or outside the published vocabulary. The registry is read by static evaluation, not by importing Odoo: a value is resolved when it is a literal, a small comprehension over a literal model list, or a call to another declaration helper in the same file. Anything else is reported instead of silently skipped. Whether an action is reachable is also decided by permission and role, so the same guard proves the authorization side: an action the backend offers must resolve a runtime authorization verdict and, when it declares a role gate, that gate must name a role from the published role vocabulary and a group the module actually declares. boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Single source for the accepted navigation action count. The acceptance lanes must not pin how many menus the product has. A menu count is only determinate once a concrete role is locked, because different roles see different contracted surfaces. boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Fail-closed consistency guard for the .agent run/goal ledger. Rule: the ledger must be internally consistent, so "goal and run status are out of sync" is a mechanically detected defect instead of a recurring manual audit. * a terminal run (completed/superseded) must not leave a non-terminal goal behind; * the active-run index must point at an existing, branch-matching, non-terminal run; * every run record keeps a canonical status and resolvable goal/record paths; * every goal declares an id, a status and, when it names a run, a resolvable path. Legacy receipts written before the goal/record schema are pinned in ``LEGACY_ARCHIVAL_RUNS``. Their bytes are historical evidence and are not rewritten to satisfy the current schema; the pin records the exact raw status so a silent lifecycle rewrite is still detected. A new legacy-shaped record that is not pinned fails this guard. Owner-kept ledger residuals are pinned with their recorded authority. The pins are ratchets: the on-disk set must equal the pinned set exactly, so a new residual cannot appear silently and a closed one must be removed here in the same change. This guard only reads the .agent ledger and never mutates it.

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Falsifiable, container-free assertions for the collection-capability rule. The list surface publishes one declared action list; ``import`` may only appear there when the caller's *effective rights* allow ``create`` on a model that has a list view and at least one importable field. boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Runtime half of the contract SLO telemetry gap. Run with: make verify.backend.contract_slo_telemetry.runtime This script is executed by ``odoo shell`` against the isolated contract-lifecycle profile (project ``sc-contract-lifecycle-v1``, database ``sc_contract_lifecycle``). It drives real ``ui.contract.v2`` deliveries through the production handler, captures the ``contractSlo`` line the production sink actually emits, and binds each observation back through the declaration consumer (``contract_slo_telemetry``), so a passing run means the runtime delivery path emitted a schema-valid, identity-complete observation rather than that a string merely appeared. Baseline first: the normal path must emit ``success`` before any injected state is treated as detected. Injection proof lives outside this script (neuter the emission boundary, prove zero lines, restore byte-identical); this script only records the healthy baseline into a machine-readable report consumed by the host-side schema guard.

That sentence only becomes decidable when it is turned into a finite, reviewable check: * every decision-shaped expression inside the frontend decision scopes (``pages`` / ``views`` / ``app``) is detected by a named rule; * every detection is either declared render/interaction, registered in this ledger with an explicit classification and an evidence pointer, or a failure; * ``contract-derived`` intent literals are verified against the *published* contract export (``docs/contract/exports/intent_catalog.json``) instead of a frozen string list, so the check stays structural rather than literal; * ``contract-projectable-gap`` entries are the actionable backlog -- frontend decisions that have no contract carrier yet but can be projected by the backend. The ledger is regenerated from this module

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Fail-closed guard for the frontend decision-authority ledger. The guard answers one decidable question: *does every frontend decision inside the declared scopes either come from the runtime contract, sit on the recorded projectable-gap backlog, or belong to the declared render/interaction half?* It fails when: * a decision-shaped expression matches a rule but is not classified (a new frontend business decision, a new capability literal gate, a new action id); * an ``invariant_zero`` rule matches anything at all; * a ``contract-derived`` intent literal is not declared in the published intent catalog export; * a ledger row cites an evidence file that no longer exists; * the committed ledger (``docs/frontend_productization/decision-authority-inventory-v1.json``) is out semantically out of sync with the live scan in either direction. Valid row line-number drift is advisory only; diagnostics report current locations. It is read-only: it never edits product code or the ledger.

Set ``FRONTEND_INDUSTRY_AGNOSTIC_ENFORCE=1`` only when the inventory has reached zero; that mode is intended for the release gate after convergence. Each finding also records the lexical role of the match. A word inside a comment or a plain string is not by itself a behavior selector, while a word used in a comparison, ternary or lookup does select structure. The role is diagnostic: it does not change ``finding_count`` or the enforcement decision, it only keeps the report from flattening "consumes a declared name" and "invents a rule" into one number.

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Mobile viewport contract guard (G4 incremental closure). R-G4-01: the SPA declares `env(safe-area-inset-*)` paddings in shell and form pages. Without `viewport-fit=cover` in the viewport meta those environment variables are always 0 on notched devices, silently disabling the safe-area handling. This guard fail-closes on: 1. index.html viewport meta missing `width=device-width`, `initial-scale=1` or `viewport-fit=cover`. 2. Any style using `env(safe-area-inset-` while viewport-fit=cover is absent (cross-file consistency). 3. `user-scalable=no` / `maximum-scale=1` regressions (accessibility floor: zoom must not be disabled).

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Runtime theme-profile switching guard. Verifies that the product-level style profile layer stays consistent: 1. profile.css declares all three SceneDesignTokenProfile ids. 2. profile.css semantic overrides match the authoritative values in kits/tokens.ts (brand color, control radius, surface radius). 3. theme.ts exposes the full profile model: 3 ids, isSceneThemeProfile and a nextThemeProfile cycle that covers every id exactly once per rotation. 4. Orthogonality: profile.css must NOT override light/dark-owned surface tokens (surface-page / surface-panel) anywhere, so switching a profile inside dark mode keeps the dark surface intact. The one sanctioned exception is the high-contrast profile's non-dark text contrast block. Exits non-zero on any violation (fail-closed).

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Fail when a list-surface claim is bound to evidence that does not support it. The page-pattern ledgers bind a conclusion to a concrete observation, e.g. ``... gates 108/108 list-surface checks ...``. A claim is only proof when the cited artifact is *archived* under a recorded identity and when its recorded gate counts equal the claimed ones. This was a real defect: ``collection.header-actions`` and ``collection.toolbar-surface`` cited ``.runtime/final-acceptance/list-surface-structure.json`` as ``316/316 gated``, but that mutable path had since been overwritten by a payment.request create/edit run whose document records ``records 12/12`` and ``gated 0/0``. The ledger therefore asserted list-surface coverage that no artifact supported — and the guard itself depended on a machine-local file that may not exist at all on another checkout. Both problems are fixed at once by binding claims to a tracked, hash-verified evidence archive (``.../rendering-detail/evidence-archive/manifest.v1.json``): * a claim must cite an artifact the archive records; * when a local copy exists its sha256 must match the archived identity, so a path that was overwritten by another run stops proving the claim;

This probe therefore measures, for one fixed identity and one fixed request, how many net container allocations each stage retains, and where inside the request they are produced. Two passes on the same identity: * an enabled pass (``gc`` on) that records the real generation-0/1/2 distribution and the dispatch time, i.e. the phenomenon to explain; * a disabled pass (``gc`` off) that wraps a curated set of existing product callables and attributes the net-retained container delta to each one with a nesting-aware exclusive split, so the sum plus an explicit residual is the whole request. boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Read-only runtime probe for assembled-cache identity invalidation (P0/P4). The record-free assembled hit returns after re-sealing; it does not re-run the entitlement, policy, action, modifier or trim projection. Its safety therefore rests on the cache key (principal groups, company, request identity) and the source token (ACL, rules, user row, business-policy definitions, code identity). This probe exercises both halves on the registered ``sc-local-dev`` / ``sc_dev_demo`` profile: * inside a savepoint, remove one group from the declared demo principal, then recompute the key and token; both must move; * inside a savepoint, change one field policy (or, when none applies, one business-config contract definition), then recompute the token; it must move. Both writes are rolled back and commit is refused. After the rollbacks the probe recomputes the baseline identities and requires them to be unchanged, so a reported invalidation cannot come from a leaked write.

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: CAP-02C-04 D1/D2: unified snapshot projection + two-phase + semantic diff. Repository Mode (``module.capability.index.v1``) and Runtime Mode (``module.runtime.facts.v1``) are projected into one traceable shape (``module.snapshot.projection.v1``). Every fact keeps its origin (``source_mode`` / ``source_module`` / ``source_ref`` / ``completeness``) and a stable ``fact_identity``. Three layers are deliberately separated: D1 phase 1 - module version / fact digest / file digests (cheap gate); D1 phase 2 - fact existence and normalized-content comparison; D2 - per-asset semantic explanation of *what* changed. D3 impact propagation is intentionally out of scope here. Odoo module contributions are preserved as sets: ``ir.model.modules`` and ``ir.model.fields.modules`` are contribution sets, never a single owner. ``model_owner`` is only ``_original_module`` (the Registry model class). An asset therefore carries ``asset_modules`` (list) rather than a flattened owner. Read-only analysis: never changes capability maturity, release state, or triggers re-certification. Un-attributable or un-parseable change is reported as ``unresolved_impact`` / ``content_unresolved``, never "no change".

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Every native object button on a workflow-adopted model is accounted for. The workflow contract publishes a subset of the native form actions. Anything the contract does not publish stays invisible to the Web -- which is the right default for a business action whose meaning nobody has declared, but a silent one: a button that really drives a state transition would simply disappear from the adopted page with no record that it was ever there. This guard makes that set explicit and fail-closed: * a native ``type="object"`` button on an adopted model whose method no profile declares must be registered in ``config/contract/native_view_undeclared_actions.v1.json`` with its nature; * an entry that no longer appears in any native view is stale and must go; * an entry whose method is now declared by a contract profile is stale too -- the registration must not outlive the gap it records. Scope note: the model set and the declared-method set both come from statically evaluating ``PROFILE_BY_MODEL`` (see ``workflow_contract_profile_loader``). The registry mixes inline literals with helper calls such as ``**_simple_approval_profiles((...))``; a regex over the source text sees only the inline hal

This probe asserts that partition against an authority that is independent of the server's own answer - the repository's locked role surface (``addons/smart_construction_core/core_extension_policy_maps.py``): * the served revision is the build the probe's contract belongs to; * every menu the locked role contract declares is delivered or explicitly denied with a ``reason_code`` - a declared entry may never disappear without an observable decision; * delivered entries carry a contract source, never a native menu tree acting as a second product-selection authority; * behaviour: ordinary roles never receive an admin route and are denied it, a contextual execution route obeys company/project scope, and the runtime never answers HTTP 500. Delivered counts are deliberately NOT pinned: a count calibrates one build against one release gate, whereas the partition identity holds for every build.

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: The entry decides the namespace; it never lets a client pick a database. ADR-007 batch C changed the mechanism this guard protects: * the path prefix (``/t/<alias>`` or ``/platform-admin``) is the only selector; * every client database hint (``X-Odoo-DB`` / ``X-DB`` / ``X-Odoo-DB-Locked`` / ``?db=``) is stripped at the entry and refused by Odoo as a conflict; * the entry stamps the namespace, audience, route version and shared secret so Odoo can verify the request came through the single public face; * the platform namespace is a declared two-layer hop: the serving entry face forwards ``/platform-admin/...`` unchanged, and only the platform duty face strips the prefix for its own Odoo (``SC_ENTRY_PLATFORM_STRIP``).

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Hardening guard: keep the browser test/probe layer off vendor-internal DOM. The adopted official template is consumed through its documented public surface (roles, semantic markers, business facts). Test and probe scripts must verify user-visible behaviour the same way. Coupling them to TDesign internal class names, transition state classes, or pixel geometry makes a green suite meaningless once the official component changes its markup, and it hides real regressions because the assertion follows the markup instead of the business fact. Enforced rules over the browser test/probe corpus: * ``transition_state_class`` (zero tolerance) Vue/transition state classes such as ``--enter-active`` or ``v-enter`` observed from a probe prove nothing about the settled page and are inherently timing dependent. * ``dom_api_playwright_pseudo`` (zero tolerance) Playwright-only selector syntax (``:visible``, ``:has-text(``, ``:text=``) passed to ``querySelector``/``querySelectorAll`` is a latent runtime error, not a passing assertion. * ``vendor_internal_selector`` (baseline, decrease-only) A literal selector that reaches a ``.t-*`` class below a non-``Sc`` root couples the probe to private TDesign i

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Static detection of two "code exists but is silently dead" defects. Both families shipped in this repository and only surfaced in production, because a plain parse of the source cannot see them. 1. Names read but never bound A helper was called but never imported, so the path raised ``NameError``. ``scripts/ci/python_syntax_check.py`` only builds an AST; it never resolves binding, so the defect stayed invisible until a user hit it. This guard walks the standard-library ``symtable`` scope tree and reports names that are referenced, are not local, are not module-level bindings and are not Python builtins -- exactly the names that raise ``NameError`` at runtime. 2. ``env.get("<model>")`` used for truthiness On an Odoo ``Environment``, ``env.get(model)`` returns an *empty recordset* when the model exists and ``None`` when it does not. Both are falsy, so ``if env.get("res.partner"):`` is always False: the model is present and the branch is still dead. That silently disabled audit writes, a capability report and several test guards. boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Lock the declared divergence between menu-layer capability reachability and the published navigation surface. ``ROLE_SURFACE_OVERRIDES`` (and the frontend navigation manifest) decide what a role actually gets on the published navigation surface. The menu XML ``groups`` declaration decides what the same role can reach at the menu/ACL layer. For several roles those two authorities deliberately disagree: the capability is reachable but the entry is intentionally not registered on the release surface. That divergence is a product decision, not a defect. It must therefore be declared explicitly in ``config/frontend/role_surface_exposure_declarations_v1.json`` and locked by this guard: any drift in either direction (a newly reachable but undocumented entry, a declared entry that quietly became reachable, a delivery-mode change, an identity group change, a new entry in the acceptance universe) fails closed until the owner re-declares it. The guard is static: it reads the acceptance entry universe, the role policy map, the role/capability group XML and the declaration file. It never relaxes ACLs, field permissions, acceptance assertions or the release navigation surface.

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Generate the global company-scope ceilings from the data-scope declaration. scripts/verify/data_scope_declarations.json is the single source: an ``enforced`` entry contributes its own anchor, a ``deferred`` group contributes its anchor for every listed model. This script turns that declaration into the ir.rule records that actually constrain access, so a new company ceiling is a one-line declaration change instead of another hand-written near-duplicate record. A ``source_bounded`` entry is deliberately *not* rendered: that model already carries the named global ir.rule the declaration points at, and emitting a second ceiling would duplicate one fact. The coverage guard verifies the named rule, so the declaration stays the single source for both paths. ``--check`` regenerates in memory and fails when the committed file differs, so the generated output can never drift from the declaration.

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Fail-closed check that every product-owned company model is accounted for. The registered 744-model registry is inspection scope, not a rewrite list. This guard reads source only (offline lane) and enforces two things: * the explicit declaration in data_scope_declarations.json is internally sound: every ``enforced`` model has a *global* ir.rule (no groups, so no group union can widen it) whose domain constrains the declared company anchor path; every ``exempt`` model names one isolation dimension and its owning module; every ``deferred`` model belongs to a group with an issue id, an anchor, an owner and an actionable reason *and* carries the same global ceiling an enforced model does (deferred records the delivery order, never the isolation), so the rule set can be regenerated from the declaration and deleting it cannot hide; every ``source_bounded`` model names the existing global ir.rule (id and file) that bounds it, that named rule is verified instead of inferred, and it must carry both isolation facts on the declared anchor - the allowed-company selector *and* the purpose authority ``user._sc_data_company_ids()``, exactly as the generated ceiling for an ``enforced`` model does;

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Guard the inventory test-scene boundary. A scene is "test-only" when its scene_key matches one of TEST_SCENE_PATTERNS or appears in TEST_SCENE_KEYS. Test-only scenes must stay at R1 to avoid leaking into product dashboards (R3 evaluation) and into business navigation/route strategies. This guard fails when: 1. a test scene is registered at R2+ (would be evaluated by product gates), or 2. a test scene is registered without an `owner_module` (must trace back to the test/runtime owner module so production releases do not adopt it), or 3. a test scene lives in a business `nav_group` other than the dedicated `others` bucket (forbidden to share nav_group with business scenes). Non-test scenes must keep their maturity at R2+ when present in the matrix (R0/R1 short-lived entry points are tracked separately in `addons/smart_construction_scene/scene_registry.py::list_scene_entries`).

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Fail-closed check that dictionary startup data never widens a scope silently. ``sc.dictionary`` carries three deliverable scopes: ``global`` (platform and industry-module reference sets), ``company`` (one customer company) and ``role``. The startup projection used to publish every non-role row under the ``__global__`` bucket, so a company-scoped configuration row reached every principal's contract. The single vocabulary now lives in ``dictionary_scope_projection``: * ``global`` maps to ``__global__`` and ``role`` to the row's own role code; * ``company`` maps to ``__global__`` **only** when ``scope_ref`` names a company in the caller's authorized company reference set, and is withheld otherwise; * any other scope has no bucket (it is dropped and counted, never promoted). This guard reads source only and enforces that both producers consume that one decision instead of re-deriving it inline, and that no producer can reintroduce the ``company -> __global__`` promotion.

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Focused behaviour tests for the reuse-first business-entry matrix entry. They lock the evidence-locality contract: the governed Make target forwards ``SC_ACCEPTANCE_OUTPUT_DIR`` even when the caller left it unset, so the entry must treat an empty or blank value as "unset" and keep writing evidence into the declared default directory instead of resolving to the repository root (``Path('') == '.'``) and leaking ``summary.json`` into the worktree. They also lock the immutability contract: the ledger records the ``summary.json`` each unit was folded from, so the default must be a per-run subdirectory of the declared location. A fixed default would let a later, narrower run overwrite an earlier run's evidence and break the ledger's source pointers, which is precisely the failure a targeted reverification would otherwise cause.

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Focused tests for the construction product layer's semantic declarations. FE-CONTRACT-RUNTIME-01 removed the payment model+field branch that wrote a literal component key. The product layer now declares *what a field means* and the contract registry names the component, so these tests lock the consumption rather than the old implementation: * every declared semantic is one ``contracts/registry/component.yaml`` declares; * the normalizer writes the component the registry resolves, and the module holds no component key of its own; * an undeclared semantic is refused -- the field keeps the component its facts resolve to instead of being rendered through an unregistered key; * the fields it does not declare are untouched; * the delivery vocabulary it hands over satisfies every term the frontend dialog model requires before it opens. The normalizer lives in an Odoo addon and is executed here through its own module-level declarations and functions, with the real contract-runtime resolver injected, so a declaration change is caught without an Odoo or browser round trip.

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Unit lock on the contract gate's declared per-case volatile response keys. The gate compares a regenerated snapshot against the tracked reference. A case whose response carries a value assigned by the producing environment (for example a database row handle) may declare that member name under ``volatile_keys``. The declaration is *per case* and must stay discriminating: it may only suppress the declared member, never anything else, and a malformed declaration must fail closed. These tests drive the real ``scripts/contract/gate_contract.sh`` with a stub export command, so they need no database and prove the declared semantics deterministically. The product-side assertions at the end pin the declaration to the single preference case and prove that the tracked reference no longer carries the environment-assigned handle.

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Offline lock for the contract SLO retention cron wiring. The retention horizon is configuration; the scheduled sweep is what actually enforces it. The store grew without bound once persistence was on because the horizon had no carrier, so this suite pins the *declaration consumption* rather than the presence of a file name: * the cron record must target the model derived from the model's own ``_name``, so a rename cannot leave the cron pointing at a model that no longer exists; * the model file must expose the called method, delegate to the pure store's prune helper, and stay fail-open; * the manifest must load the data file after the ACLs it depends on. A cron that exists but is inactive, mis-targeted, or calls a missing method is not retention, so those are failures here rather than a documentation note.

The 2026-10-09 nightly proved the gap is not theoretical: * the ``Run backend test suite per module`` step aborted on its first failing module (errexit was never disabled), so every later module - and its group coverage - was silently skipped and still reported as a pass; * ``uc4_native_lowcode`` (16 test files) was "verified" once by hand and then had no recurring gate at all; * ``scripts/ci/test_backend_test_suite_dispatch_contract.py`` existed with zero make/workflow references. Reachability tiers (deliberately conservative): * ``gated``

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Self-test for scripts/verify/frontend_industry_agnostic_audit.py. The audit exists to keep the production frontend from inventing business semantics. It flattened every occurrence of a domain word into one number, so "consumes a declared contract key" and "decides a rule from a name" looked identical in the report and the inventory could not be used to plan the cleanup. This test fixes the new lexical-role classifier: a word inside a comment or a literal must not be reported as code, and a word used in a branch must be reported as a branch. The finding count and the enforcement decision are deliberately unchanged, so the test also pins that the count still counts one finding per rule per line.

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Unit tests for the archived list-surface evidence binding guard. The guard exists because two page-pattern ledger entries once cited a mutable ``.runtime/final-acceptance/list-surface-structure.json`` path as ``316/316 gated`` after that path had been overwritten by a payment.request create/edit run (``records 12/12``, ``gated 0/0``) — and because the guard itself read that machine-local file, so it could not run at all on a checkout that lacked it. Claims now bind to a tracked, hash-verified archive. The tests lock the accepted direction (an archived identity that supports the claim) and every unsupported binding: unarchived path, overwritten local copy, non-surface schema, gates-nothing document, count mismatch, no path at all. They also lock machine-independence: an archived claim with no local copy still resolves.

The two ops entries (``scripts/ops/platform_database_register.py`` and ``scripts/ops/platform_database_lifecycle_apply.py``) are the only production callers of the platform registration model, and they are what turns a declared lifecycle state into a real environment fact. No such runtime result is claimed by these tests. These tests pin three boundaries the owner named: * the ops tool never decides a tenant, a purpose or an initialization rule on its own -- it consumes the declaration by module identity; * a request that would cut off the database serving the control plane, an unknown operation, a missing reason or a missing confirmation fails closed; * a lifecycle operation is never reported as an environment change unless the catalog readback shows the declared fact.

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Prove the backend's own action-declaration side is complete. A transition the backend lets a user execute must carry a published business purpose, because the Web is not allowed to infer one from a method name, a label or a button position. This guard reads the declaration authorities (instead of a rendered page) and fails when any of them can hand the Web a reachable action whose meaning is missing or outside the published vocabulary. The registry is read by static evaluation, not by importing Odoo: a value is resolved when it is a literal, a small comprehension over a literal model list, or a call to another declaration helper in the same file. Anything else is reported instead of silently skipped. Whether an action is reachable is also decided by permission and role, so the same guard proves the authorization side: an action the backend offers must resolve a runtime authorization verdict and, when it declares a role gate, that gate must name a role from the published role vocabulary and a group the module actually declares. A dangling or invented gate is a failure, not a warning. This proves the *declaration* side only. A native view may still contain buttons no authority regist

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Single static reader for the workflow contract profile registry. ``workflow_contract_service.PROFILE_BY_MODEL`` mixes inline literals with helper-generated entries:: PROFILE_BY_MODEL = { "payment.request": {...}, **_simple_approval_profiles(("sc.equipment.plan", ...)), } A regex over the source text only sees the inline half. A consumer that trusted such a pattern silently scanned a subset of the contract -- the failure mode that hid seven native buttons on the 25 helper-built models. This module evaluates the dict expression instead, so every profile is present however it was written. Only literal expressions are supported: an unsupported node raises :class:`ProfileSourceError` rather than returning a partial mapping, because a consumer must never silently scan a subset of the contract.

It is not deleted by the guard (that is a profile edit, not a guard decision) but it must be registered in ``config/contract/workflow_state_phase_dead_entries.v1.json`` with a reason, so
